- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment is strong.
- Underestimate prices during bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.4) — add 3–7% to forecast if sentiment is weak.
- Lagged price movements often overshoot — adjust forecast 3–5 days ahead by subtracting 1–3% from peak predictions.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overreact — cap forecast rise at 2–3% above immediate prior peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show rising prices, reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid overextension.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from bullish to bearish) triggers downward bias — reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment drops below 0.4 within 3 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate long-term trend — apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or declining.
